explain.ambiguous_overload: C++ cannot decide which version of the function to call. Make the argument type clear, for example 5.0 for a float or (int)x.
explain.array_size_not_constant: An array size must be a fixed number known before the program runs. Use a const int or #define.
explain.array_too_large: An array is too big: on Uno one array can hold at most 32767 bytes, and RAM is only 2 KB. Make it smaller.
explain.assignment_in_condition: There is = (assignment) inside a condition. To compare, write ==.
explain.break_outside_loop: break can only be used inside a loop (for, while) or a switch.
explain.cannot_convert: This value cannot be converted to the needed type. Check the types of the variable and the value.
explain.case_outside_switch: case and default labels must be inside the braces of a switch statement.
explain.case_sensitive_name: Arduino names are case-sensitive. Check the capital letters, for example pinMode, digitalWrite, Serial, HIGH.
explain.constant_overflow: A number is too big for its type and will be cut. On Uno an int holds only -32768 to 32767; use long.
explain.continue_outside_loop: continue can only be used inside a loop (for, while).
explain.division_by_zero: A division by zero: the result is undefined. Check the divisor.
explain.duplicate_case: Two case labels in the same switch have the same value. Each value may appear only once.
explain.else_without_if: This else has no if right before it. Check for a stray ; after the if condition or a misplaced brace.
explain.expected_constructor: Code is outside any function. Statements like digitalWrite(...) must be inside setup() or loop().
explain.expected_expression: A value is missing where C++ expected one, for example an empty argument, an extra comma, or a stray symbol.
explain.expected_initializer: Something is wrong right after a variable or function name, often a missing ; or ( on the line above.
explain.expected_unqualified_id: C++ expected a name here. Often a keyword is used as a name, or there is an extra symbol or semicolon before a brace.
explain.extra_closing_brace: There is an extra closing brace '}' that has no matching '{'. Remove it or add the missing '{'.
explain.flash_overflow: The program is too big for the board's flash memory. Remove unused code, long texts, or big tables.
explain.function_inside_function: A function starts inside another one; usually the previous function is missing its closing brace '}'.
explain.incompatible_assignment: Arrays cannot be assigned with =. Copy them element by element, or use strcpy for text.
explain.invalid_conversion: A value of one type is used where another type is required, for example text where a number is expected.
explain.invalid_directive: A line starting with # is not a known command. Check the spelling, for example #include or #define.
explain.invalid_operands: This operator does not work with these types, for example adding a number to a text literal. Use String(...) or print them separately.
explain.invalid_subscript: [ ] is used on something that is not an array. Check the variable and the brackets.
explain.jump_to_case_label: A variable is declared inside a case without its own braces. Wrap the case code in braces.
explain.library_not_available: This library is not installed on RoboSim. Use one of the available libraries listed in the message.
explain.low_memory: Little RAM is left for local variables. The board may behave strangely; shrink arrays or wrap Serial.print texts in F().
explain.lvalue_required: The left side of = must be a variable. To compare values use == instead of =.
explain.missing_closing_brace: A closing brace '}' is missing: every '{' needs a matching '}'. Check that each function, if and loop is closed.
explain.missing_include: The file in #include was not found. Check the spelling and capital letters, or whether the library is available.
explain.missing_parenthesis: A parenthesis is missing. Count ( and ) on this line; they must match.
explain.missing_quote: A text or character value is not closed. Every " needs a matching " on the same line, and every ' needs a matching '.
explain.missing_return_type: A declaration has no type. Put a type such as int, float or void before the name.
explain.missing_semicolon: A ; is missing at the end of the previous statement. Look at the line above the marked one.
explain.missing_semicolon_after_type: A class or struct definition must end with a semicolon after its closing brace: '};'.
explain.missing_setup_loop: Every Arduino sketch needs both void setup() and void loop(), even if one of them is empty.
explain.multiple_definition: The same function or global variable is defined twice, possibly in two tabs. Keep only one definition.
explain.narrowing_conversion: A value does not fit the type in a brace initializer, for example a float into an int. Use the right type or a cast.
explain.no_matching_function: No version of this function accepts these arguments. Check their number and types against the library documentation.
explain.no_member: This object has no function or field with that name. Check the spelling, for example Serial.println, not Serial.printn.
explain.no_return_value: A function that should return a value can reach its end without return. Add a return statement on every path.
explain.not_a_type: This word is used as a type but C++ does not know it. Check the spelling or add the #include for its library.
explain.ram_overflow: Global variables need more RAM than the board has (2 KB on Uno). Use smaller arrays, or F("text") for fixed texts.
explain.redefinition: This name is already defined. Rename one of them or remove the duplicate.
explain.return_value_in_void: A void function cannot return a value. Use plain return; or change the function type.
explain.signed_unsigned_compare: A signed and an unsigned number are compared; negative values may compare wrongly. Use the same type on both sides.
explain.statement_no_effect: This line does nothing, often == written where = was meant, or a function name without ().
explain.stray_character: There is a character C++ cannot read, often a smart quote, a Persian letter or digit, or an invisible character copied from a website. Retype it in English.
explain.string_literal_compare: Texts cannot be compared with ==. Use strcmp(a, b) == 0, or a String object.
explain.too_few_arguments: The function is called with fewer values than it needs. Compare the call with the function definition.
explain.too_many_arguments: The function is called with more values than it accepts. Remove the extra arguments.
explain.undeclared_name: This name is unknown here. Check the spelling, declare the variable before using it, or include the library that provides it.
explain.undefined_reference: A function is declared or called but its body is missing. Write the function, or check its name and parameters.
explain.uninitialized_variable: A variable is used before it gets a value, so its content is random. Give it a starting value.
explain.unsafe_source: This line is blocked for security: include only your own sketch files or Arduino libraries by name, without paths.
explain.unterminated_comment: A /* comment is never closed. Add */ where the comment should end.
explain.unused_variable: This variable is never used. Remove it, or check that you used the right name elsewhere.
explain.void_value_used: This function returns nothing (void), so its result cannot be stored or used.
